name: Jon S. Corzine

summary.text: Jon S. Corzine was chairman and chief executive of MF Global, the futures broker that collapsed in October 2011 leaving a shortfall in segregated customer funds. The CFTC sued him in 2013; on January 5, 2017 a federal court in Manhattan entered a consent order requiring him to pay a $5 million civil penalty, barring him from ever acting as an officer or employee of a futures commission merchant or registering with the CFTC, and prohibiting him from using insurance to cover the penalty. Former assistant treasurer Edith O'Brien was separately ordered to pay $500,000.

facts.claim: On January 5, 2017 the CFTC announced that a federal court in Manhattan had entered a consent order against Corzine in the CFTC's 2013 case over MF Global's misuse of nearly $1 billion in customer funds and his alleged failure to supervise diligently; he was ordered to pay a $5 million civil monetary penalty.

sources.title: Release Number 7508-17: Federal Court Orders Jon S. Corzine to Pay $5 Million Penalty in MF Global Case
Regulators Say Jon Corzine Will Pay $5 Million Penalty Over MF Global Collapse

facts.claim: Under the order Corzine may not seek or accept reimbursement or indemnification from any insurance policy for the penalty, and he undertook never to act as a principal, agent, officer, director or employee of a futures commission merchant and never to register with the CFTC in any capacity.

facts.claim: Edith O'Brien, MF Global's former assistant treasurer, was separately ordered to pay $500,000 for aiding and abetting the violations and barred from associating with a futures commission merchant or registering with the CFTC for eighteen months.

facts.claim: The consent order ended a legal matter of about five years and avoided a trial that had been set for October; Corzine had denied wrongdoing from the outset.

connections.claim: O'Brien was MF Global's assistant treasurer under Corzine's chairmanship; the same CFTC case resulted in a $500,000 penalty and an eighteen-month bar against her.

openQuestions: Site claim that Corzine paid a $5 million penalty in 2017 without admitting wrongdoing: supported (CFTC release 7508-17; NPR).

Site claim that the CFTC 'won a judgment that the firm unlawfully used customer funds' and the $1.6 billion shortfall figure: not tested here; the CFTC release refers to nearly $1 billion in misused customer funds.

Site claims about the $6.3 billion repo-to-maturity book, the October 28, 2011 $200 million transfer to JPMorgan to cover a London overdraft and JPMorgan's $100 million settlement with the trustee were not verified; no connection to JPMorgan Chase is recorded pending a source.
Henri Steenkamp's role was not researched.
